testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How long must you wait before retaking a written test after failing it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two days
questions.explanation: After failing a written test, you must wait at least two days before taking it again. If you passed tests for other endorsements, you can still take the skills tests for those endorsements.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from forming in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must have drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that collect in the tanks. They can be operated manually or automatically.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because you should always accelerate slowly no matter what
To keep control of your vehicle
To avoid going faster than the vehicle ahead
To be the last vehicle through an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep control of your vehicle
questions.explanation: Accelerating too fast on a slippery road can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: At 55 mph in ideal conditions, how far does an air brake vehicle need to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: 450 feet
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Alert other drivers when you brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: How much water is needed for hydroplaning to occur?

options.text: A large amount like a big puddle

questions.correctAnswerText: Only a small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water. You do not need a large amount of water for this to happen.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning occur?

options.text: At speeds as low as 30 mph
Most often when tire pressure is too high
Most often when tires have good tread

questions.correctAnswerText: At speeds as low as 30 mph
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or tread is worn.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a foggy area?

options.text: Stop on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights, do not pass others, and do not stop on the roadway. Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead
A minute of hitting the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down whenever visibility decreases.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: If a driver feels tired while driving, they should:

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip more quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants are dangerous because they wear off quickly and can cause extreme fatigue.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of drowsiness?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing by themselves, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Feeling hungry is not a sign of drowsiness.

questions.question: When testing a parking brake, the vehicle should:

options.text: Be placed in a low gear while the driver attempts to pull forward.
Be inspected by a professional mechanic.
Be driven while the parking brake is applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be placed in a low gear while the driver attempts to pull forward.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake, fasten your seatbelt, set the parking brake, place the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it is broken and must be fixed.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Are used to drain water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are used to drain water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If water and oil build up in the system, they damage the brakes.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight stated by the manufacturer as the loaded weight of a single vehicle
The maximum weight that can be pulled by a single vehicle
The minimum weight that can be hauled by a single vehicle
The maximum amount that can be loaded onto a single trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight stated by the manufacturer as the loaded weight of a single vehicle
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight of a vehicle plus its load as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What happens to a driver convicted of two serious traffic violations within three years?

options.text: They will lose their CDL for one week.
They will lose their CDL for at least 60 days.
They will be required to drive 10 mph slower than posted speed limits.
They will be restricted to driving only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will lose their CDL for at least 60 days.
questions.explanation: If you are convicted of two serious traffic violations within three years, you will lose your CDL for at least 60 days. Penalties are stricter for more violations.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, you should do all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route like an escape ramp, open field, or side street. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill:

options.text: You will slow to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your speed will increase.
questions.explanation: Gravity causes your speed to increase when driving downhill.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.correctAnswerText: Have an emergency plan.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for hazards. Make a plan for how you will handle each hazard if it becomes dangerous.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: You must listen to and follow the examiner's directions during the on-road test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Engage and release the parking brake.
Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Connect and disconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: The low pressure warning light is important for safe braking. After the system is charged, pump the brake pedal quickly to release air. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Add more space between your vehicle and the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add more space between your vehicle and the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead of your vehicle. This makes it easier for them to pass you safely. Speeding up is not helpful because they may continue to tailgate at the higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: A fatigued driver:

options.text: Should take over-the-counter medicines to stay awake.
May be slow to make important decisions.
Is usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slow to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: A tired driver will not see or react to hazards quickly. Fatigue makes it harder to make quick, smart decisions.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: Not getting enough sleep over time
When you want to take a nap
The time you need to prepare before driving after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: Not getting enough sleep over time
questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you do not sleep enough. You can only repay this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: When backing, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to stay out of other drivers' way.
Use a helper if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if you can.
questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. Always use a helper if possible when backing up.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Keeps the load from moving around.
Is only used for liquid cargo.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps the load from moving around.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be blocked to prevent it from sliding during transport. Shifting cargo makes steering and handling harder for the driver.

questions.question: If using a helper while backing a vehicle, where should they stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger side
In front of the driver side
On the side of the truck
Near the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the truck where you can see them. Agree on hand signals before backing, including a clear signal for "stop."

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum leakage is 3 psi in one minute. If the leak is faster, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: If driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Turn on before you cross railroad tracks.
Only turn on after you cross railroad tracks.
Only turn on near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on before you cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers before and while crossing railroad tracks. Turn them off after your vehicle is completely across the tracks.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming lights, look toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system?

options.text: Warm up the vehicle to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times, then begin driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, allow time for the air compressor to reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What may be necessary when checking automatic transmission fluid?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: On some vehicles, the engine must be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What should you do before driving in reverse?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to get it over with.
Walk around the vehicle to check for obstacles in your path.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the vehicle to check for obstacles in your path.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look for obstacles. Use both side mirrors while backing, and always back up slowly.

questions.question: What creates friction inside a brake drum?

options.text: Brake shoes and linings pushing against each other.
Brake shoes separating from the axle.
Brake shoes and linings pushing against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes and linings pushing against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction inside a brake drum is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment such as a fire extinguisher required?

options.text: Only for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have the proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and at least one properly charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is broken?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may exit the rear of the muffler.
It may cause problems with a fully loaded trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: What should you do if the roadway is covered by fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. If possible, avoid driving when fog is present.

questions.question: What does NOT need to be included in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number of stops.
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include trip dates, origin and destination, route of travel, beginning and ending odometer readings, total distance traveled, in-jurisdiction distance, and vehicle identification number. The number of stops is not required.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to change lanes during the skills test?

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if necessary to follow instructions.
Refuse to make the lane change if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic first.
questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you will make multiple lane changes. Always check traffic before changing lanes and use proper signals. Change lanes smoothly and safely.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load can shift during transit. Be careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle is back on course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Turn quickly in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Then countersteer to prevent the vehicle from skidding the opposite way. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, what should you check?

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: When checking a cargo lift during your vehicle inspection, look for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked securely.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights by looking at a reflection in a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: To check your vehicle's lights, set the parking brake and turn off the engine. Remove the key and take it with you. Turn on the low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle and check that the lights work.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping the system if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: What is the purpose of headers?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash.
questions.explanation: Front-end headers protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle, what should you check?

options.text: The vehicle is shinier than others.
The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: When you approach your vehicle before inspection, look for damage or leaning. Check under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which of these is NOT required?

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: When checking the power steering fluid during inspection, which of these is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, point out where the power steering fluid dipstick is located and show there is enough fluid in the engine compartment. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not above the full mark.
